battle.name: 韓侂胄攻金之戰
battle.theater: 江淮兩淮楚州泗州前線
battle.brief: 開禧二年（1206）正月，金使入宋議和、割地不成，宋廷發兵三路北伐：韓侂胄自將出兩淮，吳獵出蜀口，京東一路策應。兩淮大軍北進至泗、楚一線即遇金騎反推，淮西軍潰於前線，北伐遂罷。卡面的希臘火一類燃燒噴射器具，在宋廷的水軍與攻城序列中以猛火油櫃的形式延續，具體施放細節史無明文。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 這場戰爭的戰場擺在江淮南北兩條線上：主戰線是自楚州（今江蘇淮安）向北到泗州（今江蘇泗洪）一線的淮水下游渡口帶，副線是東路的京東與西路的蜀口。開戰的一方是南宋：都城行在臨安，韓侂胄以太師兼樞密使總攬北伐之事，中路主力是淮東、淮西兩軍與禁軍精銳，東路有京西沿邊軍與地方招撫司的部隊，西路由四川宣撫使吳獵統率的蜀口部隊；後勤靠兩浙轉運、江南漕運與淮南鹽貨，糧秣自江南運到楚州，再分送前線營寨與城寨。另一方是金：國都中都，樞密院掌軍，兩淮正面由河南路行台軍與泗、虹、宿等邊郡守軍抵禦，騎兵為其突擊骨幹。金廷在章宗即位之初削奪宗室與權臣之權，邊鎮指揮一度鬆散，正給了宋廷北伐的時機。開局是宋廷主動出兵，但很快由攻勢轉入金軍反攻，兩軍在淮水上下反覆拉鋸。整場戰爭的勝負關鍵既不在一城一堡，也不在一次會戰，而在兩淮的糧道與渡口能不能守住。戰事自開禧二年延續到開禧三年，中間夾着一次沒有結果的議和；兩邊的戰爭機器都是靠中原與江南的產出養着，誰的錢糧先斷，誰就先退。
countriesEn: The battlefield of this war lay on two lines north and south of the Jiang and the Huai: the main line ran from Chuzhou, today's Huai'an in Jiangsu, north to Sizhou, today's Sihong in Jiangsu, the belt of fords on the lower Huai; the subsidiary lines ran in the east through Jingdong and in the west through the Shuchuan gap. One belligerent was the Southern Song, with its capital at the itinerant court of Lin'an, Han Tuozhou holding the offices of grand preceptor and military affairs commissioner and taking charge of the northern campaign. The core of his central force was the Huai-dong and the Huai-xi armies together with picked troops of the imperial guard; the eastern line was held by the frontier troops of the Jingxi circuits and by the contingents of the local pacification commissions; the western line was the Shuchuan troops commanded by Wu Lie, the pacification commissioner of Sichuan. Supply rested on the transport districts of the two Zhejiang, the grain convoys of Jiangnan and the salt traffic of southern Huai, with grain moving from Jiangnan to Chuzhou and thence, in dribs and drabs, to the forward camps and stockades. The other belligerent was the Jin, with its capital at Zhongdu and the military affairs secretariat holding the war; on the Huai front the opposition was provided by the army of the Henan circuit and by the garrisons of the frontier prefectures of Sizhou, Hongxian and Suzhou, with cavalry as their striking core. In the early years of Zhangzong the Jin court curtailed the powers of the imperial clan and of the great ministers, and command on the frontier fell slack for a time, which handed the Song its opening. The Song opened the war on its own initiative, but it turned quickly into a Jin counter-offensive, and the two armies pulled back and forth along the Huai. The outcome of the whole campaign turned neither on any single city nor on any single battle, but on whether the supply road and the fords of the two Huais could be held. The fighting ran from the second year of the Kaixi era through the third, with one fruitless attempt at negotiation in between, and both war machines were fed by the produce of the Central Plain and of Jiangnan: whoever ran out of money and grain first would be the one to withdraw.
people: 留下姓名的，多數在宋廷一邊。韓侂胄是這場戰爭的當事人：開禧元年被起用為樞密使，主持對金用兵；他起用四川宣撫使吳獵整頓蜀口兵備，拒絕金使所提的割地條件，又密遣蘇良入金刺探，被金人擒住，金人後來以放歸蘇良為議和條件之一，他仍不從。發兵之後他自將中路出兩淮，屯兵楚州一線，多次更換前線將領，一度下令築壘自守、進攻為止，工程終以失利收場。右丞相史浩一派反對立刻用兵，主張先議和再圖恢復，是朝中主張退避的一端。樞密院都承旨蘇師旦是韓侂胄的親信，北伐的軍報與調度多經其手。宋寧宗趙擴起初對北伐抱期望，郊祀封賞都加在韓侂胄身上，兵敗之後才把樞密使撤下來。金方的主角是章宗完顏璟，他起初也願議和，及至宋廷所提條件越苛刻，廷議便轉向用兵；淮上戰線上的金軍主將，據各書記載包括完顏宗室中的完顏陳和尚。至于辛棄疾一輩主張用北方義軍內應、圖謀恢復的士人，始終沒有得到朝廷的采行，北伐的失敗使他們鼓吹的內應之法再無機會。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive are mostly on the Song side. Han Tuozhou was the principal party to the war: in the first year of the Kaixi era he was brought back into office as military affairs commissioner and took charge of the campaign against the Jin. He brought Wu Lie, the pacification commissioner of Sichuan, into the command to straighten out the Shuchuan forces, refused the terms of partition proposed by the Jin envoys, and secretly sent Su Liang into Jin territory to gather intelligence; Su Liang was seized by the Jin, and the Jin later made the return of Su Liang one of the conditions of a negotiated peace, which Han still refused. Once the army was out he took command of the central force himself in the two Huais, based his troops around Chuzhou, changed the commanders in front more than once, and at one point ordered the construction of fortified camps and the suspension of the offensive; the enterprise ended in failure. The chancellor of the right, Shi Hao, and his party opposed immediate war and argued for a negotiated settlement first with recovery to follow, and they were the wing of the court that counseled withdrawal. Su Shidan, the director of the military affairs secretariat, was Han's own man, and the reports and dispositions of the northern campaign passed largely through his hands. Emperor Ningzong, Zhao Kuan, at first expected much from the war, and the suburban sacrifices and the rewards of rank were all heaped upon Han Tuozhou; it was only after the defeats that the military affairs commission was taken from him. On the Jin side the principal was Zhangzong, Wanyan Jing, who was at first willing to negotiate, but as the Song conditions grew more exacting the court debates turned to war. The commanders of the Jin army on the Huai front, according to the books that record them, included Wanyan Zhenhe, prince of the imperial clan of the Wanyan line. Men of the stamp of Xin Qiji, who urged the use of loyalist bands in the north and a rising from within to recover the lost ground, never had their counsel taken up by the court, and the failure of the campaign killed the chance of any such rising.
kits: 卡面的希臘火，是一件以銅管噴射燃燒劑的兵器，背後是拜占庭帝國的配方機密與整套船上裝置。它的同源技術在宋廷以另一種名目存在：《武經總要》所錄的猛火油櫃，以皮革為囊、銅管為嘴，噴出的燃油用於焚燒舟船與城上的木構；那不是希臘火的原樣流傳，而是同一條燃燒技術譜系在中土的另一個分支，來源是本土的石油開採與用火的經驗。這次北伐涉及兩淮水網與沿邊城寨，舟師、攻城與焚燒器具都在宋廷的軍器序列之內，但《宋史》記述韓侂胄用兵，多詳於軍令、行軍與將帥，對火器幾乎不提，這件兵器的實際施放地點與次數都無可考。宋軍可考的其他兵器是弓弩與砲：各式步弓與強弩（後來在《武經總要》中以神臂弓之名著錄）構成射擊群，砲石與火藥投射物用於壓制城壘；攻城備有撞竿、雲梯與穴地用的鎬斧，防守靠城郭、拒馬與陷坑；持藤牌、朴刀與長槍的步軍在前，披札甲的騎兵在後。金軍的骨幹是騎兵，騎弓與輕弩之外另有重裝步卒披鐵甲，金人渡淮沿用把鐵索連舟繫成浮橋的老辦法，攻城時亦使用火器。運輸一方靠車營、牛馬，一方靠江淮的舟師與河道。兩軍在裝備上的差距，多半不在弓弩，而在攻城的火器與船隻。
kitsEn: The Greek fire shown on the card is a weapon that projects a burning charge through a bronze tube, and behind it stand the secret formula of the Byzantine empire and the whole apparatus that carried it on ships. A cognate technology existed in the Song under another name: the fierce-oil chest recorded in the Wujing Zongyao, in which a leather reservoir and a bronze pipe form a projector whose fuel is used to burn ships and the timber structures on a wall. That was not a copy of the Greek fire drifting east, but a separate branch of the same burning-technology lineage rooted in native experience of petroleum and of the use of fire. This campaign involved the watery country of the two Huais and the fortified towns along the frontier, and river craft, siege gear and incendiary devices all stood in the Song order of equipment; but the History of Song, in describing Han Tuozhou's conduct of the war, dwells on orders, marches and commanders and says almost nothing of fire weapons, so the actual points of use and the number of occasions for this weapon cannot be verified. The other Song weapons that can be traced are bows, crossbows and stone throwers: various infantry bows and strong crossbows, the latter later recorded in the Wujing Zongyao under the name of the divine-arm crossbow, made up the shooting groups, while stone and powder projectiles were used to pin walls and stockades. For attack they brought battering rams, scaling ladders and picks and mattocks for tunnelling, and relied on walls, chevaux-de-frise and pits in defence, with infantry carrying rattan shields, glaives and long spears in front and armoured cavalry behind. The backbone of the Jin army was cavalry, with riding bows and light crossbows, besides armoured heavy infantry, and the old device of lashing ships together with iron chains into a floating bridge carried the Jin across the Huai; they too used fire weapons in siege. One side moved its army on wagon laagers, oxen and horses, the other on the river craft and the waterways of the Jiang and the Huai. The gap between the two armies in materiel lay less in bows than in the fire weapons and the boats used against walls.
tactics: 兩淮一線的戰術，主軸是渡口與糧道。宋軍以楚州為樞紐，據城築寨，前推至泗州、虹縣一帶的渡口堡寨；步軍先攻據點、奪渡口，騎兵隨後推進，金人則避開正面，捨城不攻，專以大隊輕騎逼近營壘，尋找宋軍的側背與糧道所在。宋軍的弱點在於糧秣必須自江南沿漕運與河道分批前送，戰線一旦拉長，轉運的遲滯就會變成軍心的崩潰。開禧二年春戰事初起時，宋軍一度北進，把戰線推到泗、虹一帶；金騎反推之後，淮西軍在前方失去統一指揮，先鋒與後隊不相接，營壘被切斷，士卒散走，多為追騎所趕，韓侂胄自將的中軍退守楚州一線築壘自保，攻勢從此停住。蜀口一線的作法不同：蜀道險遠，糧運艱難，吳獵只能就地把兵與糧理順，先取關外要地、據險固守，得地之後難以深入關中，因而不久也奉罷兵之令。舟師方面，兩江與淮、泗之間的水路被用來輸送兵員與器械，燃燒器具與火船亦列其中，但實際交鋒多在岸上解決。金軍的另一套辦法是攻守轉換得極快：宋軍攻城時它是守方，宋軍退兵時它立刻變成攻方，以騎兵覆蓋鄉里、斷絕城寨間的道路，逼宋軍分兵守點，於是原本的攻勢被拖成無數小戰。
tacticsEn: The tactics on the line of the two Huais turned on the fords and the supply road. The Song made Chuzhou its pivot, holding the city and building stockades, and pushed forward to the fords and fortified posts around Sizhou and Hongxian. Infantry attacked the posts and took the crossings first, cavalry followed behind, while the Jin avoided the frontal approach, let the cities stand, and brought up masses of light horse to close on the camps in search of the Song flank and of the supply road. The Song weakness lay in grain that had to be moved forward from Jiangnan by convoys and river in small batches: once the front stretched out, the slowness of transport turned directly into the collapse of the army's spirit. When the war opened in the spring of the second year of Kaixi the Song pushed the line north to the Sizhou and Hongxian area, but once the Jin cavalry came back the Huai-xi army lost unified command in front, the vanguard and the rear could not be joined, the camps were cut apart, the men scattered and many were run down by the pursuing horse, and the central force Han Tuozhou commanded himself fell back on the Chuzhou line, built fortified camps and held them, from which point the offensive stood still. The Shuchuan line worked differently. The roads into Sichuan were narrow and the transport of grain hard, so Wu Lie could only set the soldiers and the grain in order on the spot, take the important posts outside the passes first and hold them behind difficult ground; once he had ground he could not drive deep into Guanzhong, and he too soon received the order to stand down. On the water, the reaches of the two rivers and of the Huai and the Si were used to move troops and equipment, with incendiary devices and fire ships listed among them, though most of the actual fighting was settled on the banks. The Jin way was to turn attack and defence over very quickly: when the Song attacked they were the defenders, and when the Song withdrew they became the attackers at once, covering the countryside with cavalry, cutting the roads between the walled towns and forcing the Song to split its force to hold scattered points, so that a single offensive was drawn out into a hundred small fights.
data: 可以核的數字不多，但有幾項夠硬。時間上：金使入宋議和在開禧二年（1206）正月，各書所記發兵月份略有出入，或云二月、或云三月，自發兵到全面罷兵歷時約二十二個月，直至嘉定元年（1208）初議和罷兵。前線的距離：楚州至泗州水陸約一百數十里，兩地直線不足八十公里；自楚州至行在臨安，漕運線在千里以上，一批糧食自江南運到前線營寨要轉手不下數次，這正是遠程北伐的難處所在。兵力方面各書沒有準數，宋軍各路合計只能說是以萬計，其中兩淮一路為主力；金軍在正面投入的兵力同樣以萬計，雙方都是傾力而出，不是一場可以靠奇襲取勝的小仗。錢的數目最清楚：紹興和議的舊額是每年銀三十萬兩、絹三十萬匹，嘉定元年議和時再增銀絹各三十萬，合計銀六十萬兩、絹六十萬匹，較戰前幾乎翻倍，這一筆正是北伐的帳單。損失與耗糧無從核實，各書所記斬獲多為概數，兵潰與被俘的規模常被略去。可以確定的是，開禧北伐之後金軍在兩淮的攻勢加強，數年之後便有嘉定四年（1211）的大舉南下，其後是靖康之難。
dataEn: The arithmetic that survives is not large, but a few items are hard. In time: the Jin envoys came to the Song to negotiate in the first month of the second year of the Kaixi era, 1206; the month in which the army was actually launched varies a little between the books, some saying the second month and some the third; and from the launching of the army to the general stand-down was about twenty-two months, running until the negotiated settlement and the withdrawal in the first year of Jiading, 1208. In distance: from Chuzhou to Sizhou was a little over a hundred li by water and road, less than eighty kilometres as the crow flies; from Chuzhou to the court at Lin'an the grain route ran well over a thousand li, and every batch of grain from Jiangnan changed hands several times on the way to the forward camps, which was precisely the difficulty of a distant northern campaign. As to numbers of men the books give no sound figures; the Song contingents can only be described as tens of thousands in total, with the two Huais carrying the main weight, and the Jin forces engaged on the front were of the same order. Both sides committed everything they had, and this was not a small war to be won by a raid. The money is the clearest item of all: the old quota fixed by the Shaoxing settlement was thirty thousand taels of silver and three hundred thousand bolts of silk a year, and when peace was made in the first year of Jiading another thirty thousand taels of silver and three hundred thousand bolts of silk were added, making sixty thousand taels of silver and six hundred thousand bolts of silk a year, close to double the pre-war figure; that sum was the bill for the campaign. Losses and the consumption of grain cannot be verified, the captures recorded in the books being round figures, and the scale of the routs and of the prisoners is usually passed over in silence. What can be established is that after the Kaixi campaign the Jin pressure in the two Huais increased, and that within a few years came the great invasion of the fourth year of Jiading, 1211, and after that the disaster of Jingkang.
cause: 打起來的緣由分三層。最外是眼前的：紹興和議之後宋金以淮水為界，宋稱叔、歲歲納銀絹，韓侂胄掌權後力主改取攻勢，開禧元年起用吳獵整頓蜀口，開禧二年正月拒絕金使所提的割地條件，北伐便由此啟動。往裡一層是金廷的變化：章宗即位後削奪宗室與權臣之權，邊鎮的指揮與後勤一時鬆懈，宋廷看準的就是這個空檔；金廷中的主戰派也不願放棄河南，一度主動遣使要求宋廷改稱為伯，等於逼戰。最深的一層在宋廷內部：韓侂胄主持北伐，一半是為了恢復河南的兵事主張，一半是藉此打擊慶元以來被打壓的勢力，把寧宗清理高宗朝舊冤的意願做成自己的功業；北方漢人區的義軍與願意內應者不斷勸進，也讓以小股奇襲改變大局的念頭格外誘人。三層疊在一起，就成了開禧二年那場戰爭的起因：時機看起來難得，兵力看起來充足，士氣看起來可用，而真正決定成敗的東西——兩淮的糧運距離與宋廷的指揮統一——恰恰沒有被算進去。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting ran in three layers. The outermost was immediate. After the Shaoxing settlement the Song and the Jin had the Huai as their border, with the Song taking the younger place and paying silver and silk every year, and once Han Tuozhou had his hands on the power he pressed for a change to the offensive. In the first year of Kaixi he brought Wu Lie in to straighten out the Shuchuan front; in the first month of the second year he rejected the terms of partition proposed by the Jin envoys, and the northern campaign was launched from that refusal. A layer deeper was the change inside the Jin court: after Zhangzong came to the throne the powers of the imperial clan and of the great ministers were curtailed, and the command and the supply on the frontier were slack for a time, and that gap was exactly what the Song was aiming at. The war party at the Jin court was in turn unwilling to give up Henan and even sent envoys to require that the Song call itself the elder, which amounted to a challenge. The deepest layer lay inside the Song court. Half of Han Tuozhou's motive was the military argument for recovering Henan; the other half was to strike at the faction that had been suppressed since the Qingyuan era and to turn the emperor's wish to clear the old injustices of the Gaozong years into a personal achievement of his own. Loyalist bands in the Chinese districts of the north and men ready to rise from within kept urging the scheme, and that made the notion of changing everything with a handful of raiding parties especially seductive. Layered together in this way, the three levels produced the cause of the war of 1206: the moment looked rare, the troops looked sufficient, the morale looked serviceable, and the two things that would really decide the outcome, the length of the grain route across the two Huais and the unity of command in the Song, were not counted at all.
impact: 北伐落空之後，宋廷的處境反而更壞。短期看，兩淮的邊防在一年多的消耗中變薄，主和的一派重新掌權，議和的時候又加了歲幣，銀六十萬兩、絹六十萬匹的年額從此落到頭上；宋金的名分也從叔侄改為伯侄，數年之後金人南下的口實與氣勢都更足。開禧三年之後，北方義軍與內應的線頭斷了，蜀口收復的關外州縣也因撤兵而復歸金人，宋廷把河南的門打開又關上，關上時比打開時更空。真正的後果在十二年後兌現：1211年完顏宗弼大軍南下，宋廷節節抵抗不住，1214年京師陷落，北宋覆亡，淮水兩岸的存量兵與儲備在開禧北伐時已花去一大半。技術上的線索也從這裡延伸：猛火油櫃這一類燃燒噴射器具在宋軍序列中站穩了腳，後來蒙古軍攻宋時把火油攻城用得更多；而蒙古西征中又從阿拉伯與波斯工程師手裡取得希臘火一系的噴射技術，兩條線在十三世紀的戰場上重新匯合，燃燒兵器從一個帝國的機密，變成橫跨歐亞的攻城手段。人物上，韓侂胄被追封衛王、諡忠毅，南宋對他的評價長期兩極，主戰的士人視他為英雄，收拾殘局的文官記住的卻是那筆加上去的歲幣。
impactEn: After the northern campaign collapsed, the Song court found itself in a worse position than before. In the short term the frontier in the two Huais had been thinned by more than a year of consumption, the party of peace took power again, and at the settlement the annual payments were increased, so that six hundred thousand taels of silver and six hundred thousand bolts of silk a year came down as a permanent charge; the standing of the Song toward the Jin also changed from uncle and nephew to elder and younger nephew, and the pretext and the momentum for a Jin invasion were both the stronger afterwards. After the third year of Kaixi the thread of the loyalist rising in the north and of the rising from within was cut, and the prefectures outside the passes that had been recovered in Sichuan went back to the Jin when the troops withdrew; the Song had opened the door to Henan and shut it again, and it was emptier when it shut than when it opened. The real consequence was cashed in twelve years later: in 1211 the army of Wanyan Zongbi came south in force, the Song could not hold them stage by stage, and in 1214 the capital fell and the Northern Song was destroyed, the stocks of men and supplies along the Huai having been spent to a large extent already in the Kaixi campaign. A technical thread also runs on from here: projectors of burning fuel of the fierce-oil chest type held their place in the Song order of battle, and the Mongol armies used oil against walls far more extensively when they came south against the Song; and in their western campaigns the Mongols took the projecting technology of the Greek fire line from Arab and Persian engineers, so that the two threads met again on the battlefields of the thirteenth century and a burning weapon that had once been the secret of a single empire became a means of siege warfare across the whole of Eurasia. As for the man, Han Tuozhou was posthumously given the title Prince of Wei and the posthumous name Zhongyi, and the Southern Song judged him for a long time in two opposite ways: the war party of scholars saw a hero, while the civil officials who had to clean up afterwards remembered the added payments.
result: 結局是三路北伐皆未成功。中路兩淮軍北進至泗、楚一線便被金騎反推，淮西軍在前線潰散，韓侂胄自將的中軍退保楚州築壘，攻勢停滯；西路吳獵收復關外階州、秦州一帶的據點，卻因糧運與退兵之令而不能守；京東一路始終沒有打成規模。開禧三年秋，韓侂胄在朝中的攻擊下罷兵，北伐結束，雙方開始議和；金人以放歸被擒的密使蘇良為由反覆拖延，條件越拖越高，終於無法成交。嘉定元年（1208）十一月，韓侂胄被以譏切朝政、與金人交通款曲等罪名撤職，隨即在臨安玉津橋一帶被政敵指使的殿前司將校刺殺，首級被送出境去送往金國，一時成為金人詔書中羞辱宋廷的字句。朝廷隨即與金議定：歲幣加至銀絹各三十萬，宋金改為伯侄之稱，韓侂胄追封衛王、諡忠毅。於是這場戰爭的結果可以這樣總結：河南寸土未得，兩淮折損無算，國庫多出一筆年貢，主戰的將領用性命付帳，北伐的志願則被後世收拾成一段可以反覆詠嘆的史話，而它真正打開的戰場，在淮水以北。
resultEn: The outcome was that all three lines of the campaign failed. The central force in the two Huais was driven back by the Jin cavalry after pushing north to the Sizhou and Chuzhou line, the Huai-xi army broke up in front, the army Han Tuozhou commanded himself fell back on Chuzhou and built fortified camps, and the offensive stood still. In the west Wu Lie recovered the posts outside the passes around Jizhou and Qinzhou, but could not hold them once the transport ran out and the order to withdraw came. The eastern line never grew to any scale. In the autumn of the third year of Kaixi Han Tuozhou was pressed by attacks in the court, stood the army down, and the campaign ended, with both sides moving into negotiation. The Jin kept the talks dragging by the return of the seized envoy Su Liang, and the terms rose as they were prolonged until nothing could be agreed. In the eleventh month of the first year of Jiading, 1208, Han Tuozhou was removed from office on charges of criticising the government and of holding secret communications with the Jin, and was shortly afterwards killed by officers of the palace guard at the Yujin Bridge outside Lin'an at the instigation of his political enemies; his head was carried out of the frontier and sent to the Jin, where it became for a time a phrase in the Jin rescripts used to shame the Song court. The court then settled with the Jin: the annual payments were raised by thirty thousand taels of silver and three hundred thousand bolts of silk, the Song and the Jin took the standing of elder and younger nephew, and Han Tuozhou was posthumously made Prince of Wei with the name Zhongyi. The result of the war can therefore be summed up in this way: not an inch of Henan was gained, the two Huais were depleted beyond counting, the treasury was given a new annual charge, the war party's commanders paid with their lives, and the intention behind the campaign was gathered up by later generations into a passage of history that could be sung and sighed over, while the battlefield it truly opened lay north of the Huai.
